articles.headline: Seahawks plan to have Sam Darnold back at practice Wednesday
articles.description: Coach Mike Macdonald also said "there is a chance" that quarterback Sam Darnold will play this week at Washington.
articles.body:
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is set to return to practice Wednesday after missing most of the team's first two games because of a glute injury, coach Mike Macdonald said Monday.

"Right now, the plan is for him to be out there in some capacity, and we'll go from there," Macdonald said. "How much, we'll see from here to Wednesday on what that number is. But right now, that's the goal."

Earlier Monday, on his Seattle Sports 710-AM radio show, Macdonald said "there is a chance" that Darnold will play this week against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium.

Darnold went down on the fifth play of the Seahawks' Sept. 9 opener and did not practice last week. After the Seahawks improved to 2-0 with a 31-7 win Sunday over the Arizona Cardinals, Macdonald said Darnold is ahead of schedule and that his timetable for returning has "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Since replacing Darnold, backup Drew Lock has completed nearly 73% of his passes while throwing four touchdown passes with zero turnovers. Lock's Total QBR of 86.4 is fourth-best among all quarterbacks through two weeks.

Asked about Lock's play, Macdonald indicated that it won't factor into the team's decision on whether Darnold starts Sunday, saying, "If Sam can play, he's going to play."

In other Seahawks injury news, Macdonald said rookie running back Jadarian Price's shoulder injury does not appear to be serious. The team's first-round pick left late in the third quarter Sunday and did not return.

"It's something we'll monitor throughout the week," Macdonald said. "Shouldn't be a long-term thing."

Price started each of the first two games while Zach Charbonnet -- Seattle's co-starter last season -- continues to work his way back from February ACL surgery. Charbonnet has to miss at least the next two games while on the physically unable to perform list, but a new PUP rule this year would allow the Seahawks to open his 21-day practice window Wednesday. Macdonald said they are still working through that possibility.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Six replacement options for Puka Nacua on Monday Night Football
articles.description: With Puka Nacua ruled out for the game against the New York Giants on Monday night, here are some potential last-minute replacements.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 21: Nacua ruled out for Monday Night Football

By Michael F. Florio

Rams' superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua has been ruled out for Monday Night Football due to a hip injury. That leaves Davante Adams as the top target for Matthew Stafford against the New York Giants.

For those fantasy managers that rolled the dice on Nacua's availability, replacement options are Malachi Fields, Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Darnell Mooney. For those who left him in the flex spot, Terrance Ferguson is an upside option that I would use over all those receivers except Fields. If you have Blake Corum that you can plug in as your flex, he is the top option.

Sept. 21: Kyler Murray clears protocol, will start Week 3

By Michael F. Florio

Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We have not seen much of Murray in a Vikings uniform, but he brings QB1 upside due to his rushing ability and the matchup.

The Bucs have allowed 234 passing yards per game, which ranks 11th highest in the NFL. That is after allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the NFL in 2025. Last week they allowed 19.72 fantasy points to Deshaun Watson, 11th-best among QBs through Sunday.

Murray was a fantasy target of mine this summer due to him being in the best system of his career, with great pass catchers around him. He has been top 12 in fantasy points per game among QBs in every year but one of his career. That is largely due to his rushing ability and highlights the safe floor he brings.

Some QBs I would start him over in Week 3 are Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Baker Mayfield and Jordan Love.

Which Commanders should you start with Daniels out?

Marcus Mariota is expected to start Week 3 for the Washington Commanders as Jayden Daniels continues to seek opinions on his dislocated left elbow. Daniels does not have a timetable as of now.

Mariota started eight games for the Commanders last season, averaging 200 passing yards and 32 rushing yards per game. He threw 10 touchdowns and added another with his legs.

Mariota is not someone fantasy managers should be looking to force into their lineups. He is more an option for those in superflex leagues who now find themselves in a pinch. He brings a safer floor than you might expect, thanks to the rushing numbers, but falls far short of Daniels' ceiling.

articles.headline: Cardinals CB Will Johnson (neck) could miss rest of season
articles.description: Cardinals starting cornerback Will Johnson could miss the rest of the regular season after suffering a neck injury against the Seahawks on Sunday.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals starting cornerback Will Johnson could miss the rest of the regular season after suffering a neck injury against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.

Coach Mike LaFleur made the announcement during his news conference Monday, adding that he didn't have any more information and wasn't sure if the 2025 second-round pick out of Michigan will need surgery.

Johnson left the game in the second half, but it was unclear when he suffered the injury. The Seahawks pulled away over the final two quarters for a 31-7 win.

"Will's got a neck -- potentially could miss the whole season," LaFleur said. "You're sick for Will, for obvious reasons. The person over the player. And his teammates are sick for him, too. But it's ball and we move on."

Johnson started the first two games of the season and was emerging as a key player in the Cardinals' defense. He has eight tackles, one pass defended and one fumble recovery this season.

Veteran Starling Thomas is in line to get more playing time without Johnson in the lineup.

"Star's played a lot of football here, Star's played good football and I think Star's in a good spot headspace-wise," LaFleur said.

LaFleur also said that cornerback Max Melton would be day-to-day after sustaining a toe injury Sunday. The Cardinals play on the road against the San Francisco 49ers next Sunday.

articles.description: Rounding up the top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
articles.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Monday night fits

Playing in his first game in over 900 days, Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald wore a simple black jacket and shorts with glasses on. The player he'll be looking to bring down, New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart, rocked a bomber jacket from the brand Nahmias and camouflage pants.

Here are the tops looks from "Monday Night Football."

Sunday night drip

Indianapolis Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner might have had the best outfit ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Buckner wore a navy and black silk suit made by Gentleman's Playbook. It was a bold and unique choice.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce also showed up in style with a Louis Vuitton collarless jacket and matching belt. His teammate, Patrick Mahomes, rocked Adidas from head to toe with Oakley sunglasses.

Here are the top fits ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Commanders' rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was among the best dressed players during the arrivals for the Sunday afternoon games. Styles arrived in a grey suit, with his initials embroidered on the collar in gold.

articles.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for 'MNF' vs. Giants
articles.description: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua will be active/will not be active on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua will not be active for "Monday Night Football" against the New York Giants.

Nacua was added to the Rams' injury report on Friday with a hip injury. On Saturday, McVay said Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin and would not practice that day.

McVay said the Rams were "being smart" with Nacua because he is a skill player. The head coach also said Nacua's injury is separate from the psoas injury that caused him to miss time during training camp.

McVay said that day that while Nacua practiced on Thursday, he "didn't feel totally like himself [with] his ability to be able to kind of open up and really hit full speed."

In the Rams' season opener, Nacua led the Rams with five catches for 74 yards on nine targets.

Rams wide receiver Jordan Whittington, who was added to the injury report Friday with a quad injury, is also inactive.

articles.headline: Chargers placing TEs David Njoku, Charlie Kolar on IR
articles.description: The Chargers are placing tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar on injured reserve, coach Jim Harbaugh announced Monday.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif -- The Los Angeles Chargers are placing tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar on injured reserve, coach Jim Harbaugh announced Monday.

The moves, which will sideline both players for at least four games, will leave the Chargers with one tight end -- Oronde Gadsden -- on the active roster.

Njoku was carted off the field in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders with a fibula injury. Kolar has a forearm injury.

The Chargers could fill the void at tight end by turning to their practice squad, where they currently have two tight ends: Evan Svoboda and Patrick Herbert, a brother of quarterback Justin Herbert.

It's hard to overstate the importance of Kolar and Njoku, two tight ends who thrive as blockers, in an offense that relies heavily on tight ends to block in the rushing offense. General manager Joe Hortiz spent more money on outside free agents at tight end than any other position.

The injuries are a major blow to an already struggling offense that has looked helplessly lost for the first two weeks.

Kolar had played 68 snaps and Njoku 40 to Gadsden's 34, despite Kolar and Njoku exiting Sunday's game early with injuries. Gadsden is best in the passing game and scored a touchdown Sunday but struggles as a run blocker.

"A lot of confidence in Oronde's game," Harbaugh said Monday. "So many things that he does well."

Harbaugh also said that starting left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) will "miss some time." Both exited Sunday's loss early.

Trey Pipkins III, who rotated at left guard with Awosika in Week 1, would be in line to start, but he missed Sunday's game with a knee injury. Harbaugh said that Trevor Penning will start at left guard if Pipkins isn't healthy enough to go next Sunday.

The injuries mean that five of the Chargers' eight free agent signings will now miss games: center Tyler Biadasz (season-ending ACL injury), Njoku, Kolar, Tomlinson and Awosika -- essentially five starters. Njoku appeared to get injured while blocking for running back Omarion Hampton. The entire team came out on the field to give Njoku well wishes as he exited on a cart.

The Chargers signed Njoku to a one-year deal in May after he spent his first nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns. Kolar signed a three-year, $24.3 million contract with the Chargers in March after he spent his first four seasons with the Baltimore Ravens.

Njoku has eight receptions for 67 yards this season, while Kolar has three receptions for 21 yards.

The Chargers are 0-2 after upset losses at home to the Arizona Cardinals and Raiders. Coming into this season, ESPN's Football Power Index gave the Chargers the fifth-highest odds to win the Super Bowl.

articles.headline: Sources: Cubs' Bregman suffered facial fractures from foul ball
articles.description: Chicago Cubs star Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
articles.body:
Chicago Cubs star Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.

Bregman will not undergo surgery and is hopeful to return in the postseason.

In the fourth inning of the Cubs' 9-1 win over the Reds in Cincinnati, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward Chicago's dugout with a hand covering the left side of his face.

Bregman was escorted by an athletic trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face.

"He got hit in the left cheekbone essentially, under the eye," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said after the game. "He was bleeding from his nose a little. There's some swelling. It's a terrible, terrible accident. We hope he's OK."

Bregman was hospitalized in the Cincinnati area to undergo tests, but posted on Instagram earlier Monday that he was back in Chicago.

articles.description: Could Lens winger Mezian Mesloub be Manchester United's latest teenage signing? Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United have lined up 16-year-old Lens winger Mezian Mesloub to replace JJ Gabriel, while Borussia Dortmund forward Maximilian Beier is on the radar of Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United have lined up Lens winger Mezian Mesloub as a potential long-term target, TEAMtalk reports. Scouts from United, Arsenal, Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain, and Monaco have tracked the 16-year-old, while Red Devils executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox continue efforts to convince JJ Gabriel to stay.

- Arsenal are monitoring Borussia Dortmund forward Maximilian Beier as a potential attacking reinforcement, TEAMtalk has revealed. Gunners scouts have been impressed by the 23-year-old's versatility across the frontline during their visits to monitor Ethan Nwaneri's loan spell at the German club.

- Real Madrid are assessing a move for Manchester United youngster Gabriel, according to Diario AS. Sources have told ESPN that the 15-year-old has indicated his desire to leave Old Trafford, prompting contact from Real Madrid while they evaluate eligibility requirements, with Barcelona and Bayern Munich also competing for his signature.

- Tottenham Hotspur could renew their pursuit of Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White in January, according to Football Insider. Spurs remain interested in the 26-year-old after attempting to sign him in the summer of 2025, with potential reinforcements being assessed following a difficult start to the season, but could face paying a fee of £125 million. By contrast, the England international has started the campaign strongly, registering three goal involvements in five Premier League outings.

- Atlético Madrid are set to revive their pursuit of Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Ibrahim Maza, according to Goal. The 20-year-old Algeria international's transfer could command a fee of around €70 million, though Leverkusen remain determined to retain him and are working on a contract extension with a pay rise.

Other rumors

- Liverpool could revive their interest in Brighton & Hove Albion winger Yankuba Minteh in January after seeing a €60 million bid rejected over the summer. (Sport Witness)

- The Reds have also held talks with Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, 22, over a move. (Caught Offside)
